# Hoja de ruta

Ideas que no cupieron en la versión actual, sin orden prometido. Son direcciones, no compromisos; un issue o un pull request es la mejor forma de adelantar una.

Una versión de integridad y seguridad, sin funciones grandes nuevas: un commit en verde exige el workflow obligatorio del repositorio, un fetch fallido detiene el despacho, el catálogo no puede nombrar una herramienta fuera de la carpeta de herramientas ni cambiar `dry_run`/`ref`, y un lote sin comprobación de commit registrada ya no se ofrece para firmar; `act` se queda dentro del espacio de trabajo y Stop termina todo el árbol de procesos y los contenedores de la ejecución; el modo red puede servir HTTPS, bloquea los tokens erróneos y solo acepta IPv4; el webhook rechaza reenvíos e inundaciones; el servidor MCP sobrevive a mensajes mal formados; `max_per_hour` cuenta mensajes; los ajustes se guardan bajo un bloqueo; el token guardado llega solo a `gh`; `--doctor` avisa de combinaciones peligrosas; la prueba de instalación limpia es una etapa propia del control de calidad de la publicación.

Pruebas de aislamiento de la edición lite y de la demo, ninguna petición de red cuando la comprobación de versión está apagada o la instalación está aislada, un README que empieza por la elección del lanzador, `--doctor --json`, una barra persistente para el modo red, la Ayuda y sus documentos en ocho idiomas, y las funciones opcionales (modo red, un token guardado por el monitor, acciones sobre GitHub, `act`, copia local de artefactos, runners propios, OpenTelemetry, FinOps por etiquetas de job); véase el registro de cambios y `ADVANCED.md`.

Lo que la 1.6.4 no alcanzó, y por qué:

- **Decidido, no hecho en la 1.6.5** (la versión está cerrada a integridad y seguridad): el aviso activo a una IA externa (apagado por defecto, una primera confirmación por proveedor, solo los campos ya filtrados de la lista cerrada, un tope de llamadas y de coste por hora, la clave por el nombre de una variable de entorno, y la IA nunca ejecuta una acción) con su variante de comando saliente (lista cerrada, sin shell); capturas nuevas (`tools/make_screenshots.py --web` no produjo salida en la máquina de la publicación, así que se hacen a mano: arranca `--demo`, abre la página y guarda una captura por pestaña); y los repositorios de varios propietarios en una sola página.
- **Varios propietarios en una página**: el monitor identifica un repositorio solo por su nombre (ejecuciones, centinela, caché, exportaciones), así que dos propietarios con un repositorio del mismo nombre se mezclarían. Las organizaciones se listan y cada una se vigila con su propio monitor (`github_owner`). Hacerlo en una página exige poner el propietario en cada identificador.
- **El informe de facturación con un login que pueda leerlo**: la respuesta real de un login sin el permiso `user` es «no encontrado» y el monitor vuelve a la estimación (comprobado); las cifras en sí no se han comparado con una cuenta de facturación.
- **Los precios de los runners grandes** de `quotas.json` salen de la memoria de la lista pública de precios y están marcados como no verificados; compáralos con la página de facturación de GitHub y edita el fichero.
- **`gh copilot`**: sus banderas se comprueban con `gh copilot -- --help`, que necesita la línea de comandos de Copilot; aquí no está instalada, así que siguen sin verificar.
- **Notificaciones, webhook, Enterprise Server y los ejemplos de servicio** contra servicios reales: `tools/manual_check_live.py` los comprueba a mano; necesitan tus canales y equipos, así que no se ejecutaron aquí.
- **La aplicación de terminal** edita los ajustes sencillos y muestra el estado de la IA; la explicación de un workflow en rojo concreto y la edición de listas y mapas siguen en la página.
- **Una comprobación de versión nueva que descargue o instale**: nunca; el monitor solo avisa.

- **Más adaptadores de notificación**: ntfy, Microsoft Teams y correo mediante un relé local.
- **Varias cuentas en una página**: hoy cada cuenta funciona con su propio monitor.
- **Telemetría de hardware de los runners** mediante un agente: hoy solo se lee un endpoint opcional de node exporter.
Ideas que necesitan una decisión antes

- Una pantalla de acceso para la página, de modo que el modo red no requiera escribir una vez el token de acceso. Hoy la respuesta es el token de acceso y, para Internet, un proxy inverso con autenticación (véase `monitor/docs/DEPLOYMENT.md`).
- Leer en la página los registros de un paso fallido, con la misma limpieza que aplica el asistente de IA.

# Roadmap

Ideen, die nicht in die aktuelle Version passten, ohne versprochene Reihenfolge. Es sind Richtungen, keine Zusagen; ein Issue oder ein Pull Request ist der beste Weg, eine voranzubringen.

Ein Release für Integrität und Sicherheit, ohne große neue Funktion: Ein grüner Commit braucht den erforderlichen Workflow des Repositorys, ein fehlgeschlagener Fetch stoppt den Start, der Katalog kann kein Werkzeug außerhalb des Werkzeugordners nennen und `dry_run`/`ref` nicht ändern, und ein Stapel ohne aufgezeichnete Commit-Prüfung wird nicht mehr zum Signieren angeboten; `act` bleibt im Arbeitsbereich und Stopp beendet den ganzen Prozessbaum samt Containern des Laufs; der Netzwerkmodus kann HTTPS liefern, sperrt falsche Token und akzeptiert nur IPv4; der Webhook lehnt Wiederholungen und Fluten ab; der MCP-Server übersteht fehlerhafte Nachrichten; `max_per_hour` zählt Nachrichten; Einstellungen werden unter einer Sperre gespeichert; das gespeicherte Token erreicht nur `gh`; `--doctor` warnt vor gefährlichen Kombinationen; der Test der sauberen Installation ist eine eigene Stufe der Release-Prüfung.

Isolationstests der Lite-Edition und der Demo, keinerlei Netzwerkanfrage, wenn die Versionsprüfung aus ist oder die Installation abgeschottet ist, ein README, das mit der Wahl des Starters beginnt, `--doctor --json`, eine dauerhafte Leiste für den Netzwerkmodus, die Hilfe und ihre Dokumente in acht Sprachen sowie die optionalen Funktionen (Netzwerkmodus, ein vom Monitor gespeichertes Token, Aktionen auf GitHub, `act`, lokale Kopie von Artefakten, eigene Runner, OpenTelemetry, FinOps nach Job-Labels); siehe Änderungsprotokoll und `ADVANCED.md`.

Was 1.6.4 nicht erreicht hat, und warum:

- **Beschlossen, in 1.6.5 nicht erledigt** (das Release ist auf Integrität und Sicherheit beschränkt): die aktive Meldung an eine externe KI (standardmäßig aus, eine erste Bestätigung je Anbieter, nur die bereinigten Felder der geschlossenen Liste, ein Limit für Aufrufe und Kosten pro Stunde, der Schlüssel über den Namen einer Umgebungsvariable, und die KI führt nie eine Aktion aus) samt der Variante mit ausgehendem Befehl (geschlossene Liste, keine Shell); neue Screenshots (`tools/make_screenshots.py --web` lieferte auf dem Release-Rechner keine Ausgabe, sie werden also von Hand gemacht: `--demo` starten, die Seite öffnen und pro Reiter eine Aufnahme speichern); und die Repositories mehrerer Eigentümer auf einer Seite.
- **Mehrere Besitzer in einer Seite**: Der Monitor erkennt ein Repository allein an seinem Namen (Läufe, Wächter, Cache, Exporte); zwei Besitzer mit gleichnamigem Repository würden sich vermischen. Organisationen werden aufgelistet und jede von einem eigenen Monitor überwacht (`github_owner`). In einer Seite bräuchte jede Kennung den Besitzer.
- **Der Abrechnungsbericht mit einem Login, der ihn lesen darf**: Die echte Antwort für einen Login ohne den Scope `user` ist „nicht gefunden“, und der Monitor fällt auf die Schätzung zurück (geprüft); die Zahlen selbst wurden nicht mit einem Abrechnungskonto verglichen.
- **Die Preise größerer Runner** in `quotas.json` stammen aus dem Gedächtnis der öffentlichen Preisliste und sind als ungeprüft markiert; vergleiche sie mit der Abrechnungsseite von GitHub und bearbeite die Datei.
- **`gh copilot`**: Seine Optionen werden mit `gh copilot -- --help` geprüft, was die Copilot-Kommandozeile braucht; sie ist hier nicht installiert, die Optionen bleiben ungeprüft.
- **Benachrichtigungen, Webhook, Enterprise Server und die Dienstbeispiele** gegen echte Dienste: `tools/manual_check_live.py` prüft sie von Hand; sie brauchen deine Kanäle und Hosts und wurden hier nicht ausgeführt.
- **Die Terminal-Anwendung** bearbeitet die einfachen Einstellungen und zeigt den KI-Status; die Erklärung eines einzelnen roten Workflows und das Bearbeiten von Listen und Maps bleiben in der Seite.
- **Eine Prüfung auf neue Versionen, die herunterlädt oder installiert**: niemals; der Monitor sagt es nur.

- **Weitere Benachrichtigungsadapter**: ntfy, Microsoft Teams und E-Mail über ein lokales Relay.
- **Mehrere Konten in einer Seite**: Heute läuft jedes Konto in einem eigenen Monitor.
- **Hardware-Telemetrie der Runner** über einen Agenten: Heute wird nur ein optionaler Node-Exporter-Endpunkt gelesen.
Ideen, die zuerst eine Entscheidung brauchen

- Eine Anmeldeseite, damit der Netzwerkmodus kein einmal eingegebenes Zugriffstoken braucht. Heute ist die Antwort das Zugriffstoken und, fürs Internet, ein Reverse-Proxy mit Authentifizierung (siehe `monitor/docs/DEPLOYMENT.md`).
- Die Logs eines fehlgeschlagenen Schritts in der Seite lesen, mit derselben Bereinigung wie beim KI-Assistenten.

# Feuille de route

Des idées qui n'ont pas tenu dans la version actuelle, sans ordre promis. Ce sont des directions, pas des engagements ; une issue ou une pull request est la meilleure façon d'en faire avancer une.

Une version d'intégrité et de sécurité, sans grosse nouveauté : un commit vert exige le workflow obligatoire du dépôt, un fetch en échec arrête le lancement, le catalogue ne peut pas nommer un outil hors du dossier des outils ni changer `dry_run`/`ref`, et un lot sans vérification de commit enregistrée n'est plus proposé à la signature ; `act` reste dans l'espace de travail et Stop termine tout l'arbre de processus et les conteneurs de l'exécution ; le mode réseau peut servir du HTTPS, bloque les jetons erronés et n'accepte que l'IPv4 ; le webhook refuse rejeux et inondations ; le serveur MCP survit aux messages mal formés ; `max_per_hour` compte les messages ; les réglages sont enregistrés sous verrou ; le jeton conservé n'atteint que `gh` ; `--doctor` signale les combinaisons dangereuses ; le test d'installation propre est une étape à part du contrôle de publication.

Tests d'isolation de l'édition lite et de la démo, aucune requête réseau quand la vérification de version est désactivée ou l'installation isolée, un README qui commence par le choix du lanceur, `--doctor --json`, une barre persistante pour le mode réseau, l'aide et ses documents en huit langues, et les fonctions optionnelles (mode réseau, un jeton conservé par le moniteur, actions sur GitHub, `act`, copie locale des artefacts, runners auto-hébergés, OpenTelemetry, FinOps par étiquettes de job) ; voir le journal des modifications et `ADVANCED.md`.

Ce que la 1.6.4 n'a pas atteint, et pourquoi :

- **Décidé, non fait dans la 1.6.5** (la version est limitée à l'intégrité et à la sécurité) : l'avis actif à une IA externe (désactivé par défaut, une première confirmation par fournisseur, seulement les champs déjà filtrés de la liste fermée, un plafond d'appels et de coût par heure, la clé par le nom d'une variable d'environnement, et l'IA n'exécute jamais d'action) avec sa variante de commande sortante (liste fermée, sans shell) ; de nouvelles captures (`tools/make_screenshots.py --web` n'a rien produit sur la machine de publication : elles se font à la main, en lançant `--demo`, en ouvrant la page et en enregistrant une capture par onglet) ; et les dépôts de plusieurs propriétaires sur une seule page.
- **Plusieurs propriétaires dans une page** : le moniteur identifie un dépôt par son seul nom (exécutions, sentinelle, cache, exports) ; deux propriétaires ayant un dépôt du même nom se mélangeraient. Les organisations sont listées et chacune est surveillée par son propre moniteur (`github_owner`). Le faire dans une page demande le propriétaire dans chaque identifiant.
- **Le rapport de facturation avec un compte qui peut le lire** : la vraie réponse pour un compte sans la portée `user` est « introuvable » et le moniteur retombe sur l'estimation (vérifié) ; les chiffres eux-mêmes n'ont pas été comparés à un compte de facturation.
- **Les prix des gros runners** de `quotas.json` viennent de la mémoire de la grille tarifaire publique et sont marqués non vérifiés ; comparez-les à la page de facturation de GitHub et modifiez le fichier.
- **`gh copilot`** : ses options se vérifient avec `gh copilot -- --help`, qui exige la ligne de commande Copilot ; elle n'est pas installée ici, donc elles restent non vérifiées.
- **Notifications, webhook, Enterprise Server et exemples de service** face à des services réels : `tools/manual_check_live.py` les vérifie à la main ; ils demandent vos canaux et hôtes, ils n'ont donc pas été lancés ici.
- **L'application de terminal** modifie les réglages simples et montre l'état de l'IA ; l'explication d'un workflow rouge précis et l'édition des listes et tables restent dans la page.
- **Une vérification de nouvelle version qui télécharge ou installe** : jamais ; le moniteur ne fait que le dire.

- **Plus d'adaptateurs de notification** : ntfy, Microsoft Teams et e-mail via un relais local.
- **Plusieurs comptes dans une page** : aujourd'hui chaque compte tourne dans son propre moniteur.
- **Télémétrie matérielle des runners** via un agent : aujourd'hui seul un point d'accès optionnel de node exporter est lu.
Idées qui demandent d'abord une décision

- Un écran de connexion pour la page, afin que le mode réseau n'exige plus de saisir une fois le jeton d'accès. Aujourd'hui la réponse est le jeton d'accès et, pour Internet, un reverse proxy avec authentification (voir `monitor/docs/DEPLOYMENT.md`).
- Lire dans la page les journaux d'une étape en échec, avec le même nettoyage que l'assistant IA.

# Roadmap

Idee che non sono entrate nella versione attuale, senza ordine promesso. Sono direzioni, non impegni; una issue o una pull request è il modo migliore per farne avanzare una.

Una versione di integrità e sicurezza, senza grandi novità: un commit verde richiede il workflow obbligatorio del repository, un fetch fallito ferma l'avvio, il catalogo non può indicare uno strumento fuori dalla cartella degli strumenti né cambiare `dry_run`/`ref`, e un lotto senza verifica del commit registrata non viene più proposto alla firma; `act` resta nell'area di lavoro e Stop termina l'intero albero di processi e i container dell'esecuzione; la modalità rete può servire HTTPS, blocca i token errati e accetta solo IPv4; il webhook rifiuta replay e inondazioni; il server MCP sopravvive ai messaggi malformati; `max_per_hour` conta i messaggi; le impostazioni si salvano sotto blocco; il token conservato arriva solo a `gh`; `--doctor` segnala le combinazioni pericolose; il test di installazione pulita è una fase a sé del controllo di pubblicazione.

Test di isolamento dell'edizione lite e della demo, nessuna richiesta di rete quando il controllo versione è spento o l'installazione è isolata, un README che inizia con la scelta del lanciatore, `--doctor --json`, una barra persistente per la modalità rete, la Guida e i suoi documenti in otto lingue, e le funzioni opzionali (modalità rete, un token conservato dal monitor, azioni su GitHub, `act`, copia locale degli artefatti, runner self-hosted, OpenTelemetry, FinOps per etichette dei job); vedi il registro delle modifiche e `ADVANCED.md`.

Ciò che la 1.6.4 non ha raggiunto, e perché:

- **Deciso, non fatto nella 1.6.5** (la versione è limitata a integrità e sicurezza): l'avviso attivo a una IA esterna (spento di default, una prima conferma per fornitore, solo i campi già filtrati dell'elenco chiuso, un tetto di chiamate e di costo all'ora, la chiave tramite il nome di una variabile d'ambiente, e l'IA non esegue mai un'azione) con la sua variante di comando in uscita (elenco chiuso, senza shell); nuove schermate (`tools/make_screenshots.py --web` non ha prodotto output sulla macchina di pubblicazione, quindi si fanno a mano: avvia `--demo`, apri la pagina e salva una cattura per scheda); e i repository di più proprietari in una sola pagina.
- **Più proprietari in una pagina**: il monitor identifica un repository solo dal nome (esecuzioni, sentinella, cache, esportazioni), quindi due proprietari con un repository dello stesso nome si mescolerebbero. - **Il rapporto di fatturazione con un login che può leggerlo**: la risposta reale per un login senza lo scope `user` è «non trovato» e il monitor torna alla stima (verificato); le cifre non sono state confrontate con un account di fatturazione.
- **I prezzi dei runner grandi** in `quotas.json` vengono dalla memoria del listino pubblico e sono segnati come non verificati; confrontali con la pagina di fatturazione di GitHub e modifica il file.
- **`gh copilot`**: le sue opzioni si verificano con `gh copilot -- --help`, che richiede la riga di comando di Copilot; qui non è installata, quindi restano non verificate.
- **Notifiche, webhook, Enterprise Server ed esempi di servizio** su servizi reali: `tools/manual_check_live.py` li controlla a mano; servono i tuoi canali e host, quindi qui non sono stati eseguiti.
- **L'applicazione da terminale** modifica le impostazioni semplici e mostra lo stato dell'IA; la spiegazione di un singolo workflow rosso e la modifica di liste e mappe restano nella pagina.
- **Un controllo di nuova versione che scarichi o installi**: mai; il monitor si limita ad avvisare.

- **Altri adattatori di notifica**: ntfy, Microsoft Teams ed e-mail tramite un relay locale.
- **Più account in una pagina**: oggi ogni account gira nel proprio monitor.
- **Telemetria hardware dei runner** tramite un agente: oggi si legge solo un endpoint opzionale di node exporter.

- Una schermata di login per la pagina, così la modalità rete non richiede di digitare una volta il token di accesso. Oggi la risposta è il token di accesso e, per Internet, un reverse proxy con autenticazione (vedi `monitor/docs/DEPLOYMENT.md`).

1-6-5-で完了したこと
1.6.5 で完了したこと

大きな新機能のない、整合性とセキュリティのリリースです。緑のコミットにはリポジトリの必須ワークフローが必要で、fetch の失敗は起動を止め、カタログはツールフォルダー外のツールや `dry_run`/`ref` の変更を指定できず、コミット確認が記録されていないバッチは署名に提示されません。`act` はワークスペース内に留まり、Stop は実行のプロセスツリー全体とコンテナーを終了します。ネットワークモードは HTTPS を提供でき、誤ったトークンをロックし、IPv4 のみ受け付けます。Webhook はリプレイと大量送信を拒否し、MCP サーバーは不正なメッセージに耐え、`max_per_hour` はメッセージ数を数え、設定はロック下で保存され、保存したトークンは `gh` にのみ渡り、`--doctor` が危険な組み合わせを警告し、クリーンインストールのテストはリリース検査の独立した段階になりました。
1-6-4-で完了したこと
1.6.4 で完了したこと

LITE版とデモの分離テスト、更新確認がオフまたはエアギャップ環境のときはネットワーク要求を一切出さないこと、ランチャーの選択から始まる README、`--doctor --json`、ネットワークモード用の常時表示バー、ヘルプとその文書の8言語対応、そしてオプション機能(ネットワークモード、モニターが保持するトークン、GitHub への操作、`act`、アーティファクトのローカルコピー、セルフホストランナー、OpenTelemetry、ジョブのラベルによる FinOps)。変更履歴と `ADVANCED.md` を参照してください。
次に
次に

1.6.4 で届かなかったことと理由:

- **決定済みだが 1.6.5 では未実施**（このリリースは整合性とセキュリティに限定）: 外部 AI へのアクティブな通知（既定でオフ、プロバイダーごとの初回確認、閉じたリストのうち除去済みのフィールドのみ、1 時間あたりの呼び出し数とコストの上限、環境変数名によるキー、AI は決してアクションを実行しない）と、その送信コマンド版（閉じたリスト、シェルなし）。新しいスクリーンショット（`tools/make_screenshots.py --web` はリリース用マシンで出力を生成しなかったため手作業：`--demo` を起動し、ページを開いてタブごとにキャプチャを保存）。複数の所有者のリポジトリを 1 ページに表示すること。
- **1つのページで複数のオーナー**: モニターはリポジトリを名前だけで識別します(実行、センチネル、キャッシュ、エクスポート)。同名のリポジトリを持つ2つのオーナーが混ざってしまいます。組織は一覧表示し、それぞれ専用のモニターで監視します(`github_owner`)。1ページで行うには、すべての識別子にオーナーが必要です。
- **請求レポートを読めるログインでの確認**: `user` スコープのないログインの実際の応答は「見つからない」で、モニターは推定に戻ります(確認済み)。数値そのものは請求アカウントと照合していません。
- **大型ランナーの料金**(`quotas.json`)は公開料金表の記憶に基づく未検証の値です。GitHub の請求ページと比較してファイルを編集してください。
- **`gh copilot`**: フラグは `gh copilot -- --help` で確認しますが、Copilot コマンドラインが必要です。ここには未インストールのため未検証のままです。
- **通知、Webhook、Enterprise Server、サービスの例**の実サービスでの確認: `tools/manual_check_live.py` で手動確認できます。皆様のチャネルとホストが必要なため、ここでは実行していません。
- **ターミナルアプリ**は簡単な設定の編集とAIの状態表示に対応します。個別の赤ワークフローの説明や、リスト・マップの編集はページ側にあります。
- **ダウンロードやインストールまで行う新バージョン確認**: 行いません。モニターは通知するだけです。
将来
将来

- **通知アダプターの追加**: ntfy、Microsoft Teams、ローカルリレー経由のメール。
- **1ページで複数アカウント**: 現在は各アカウントが専用のモニターで動作します。
- **エージェントによるランナーのハードウェアテレメトリ**: 現在は任意の node exporter エンドポイントのみ読み取ります。
先に判断が必要なアイデア
先に判断が必要なアイデア

- ページのログイン画面(ネットワークモードでアクセストークンを一度入力する手間をなくすため)。現在の答えはアクセストークン、インターネット向けには認証付きリバースプロキシです(`monitor/docs/DEPLOYMENT.md` を参照)。
- 失敗したステップのログを、AIアシスタントと同じ整形でページ内に表示すること。
zh:
# 路线图

当前版本放不下的想法,不承诺顺序。它们是方向而非承诺;推动其中之一的最佳方式是提交 issue 或 pull request。

一次完整性与安全版本，没有大型新功能：绿色提交需要仓库的必需工作流，fetch 失败会阻止触发，目录不能指定工具文件夹之外的工具或更改 `dry_run`/`ref`，没有记录提交校验的批次不再提供签名；`act` 留在工作区内，停止会结束运行的整个进程树和容器；网络模式可提供 HTTPS，锁定错误令牌，仅接受 IPv4；Webhook 拒绝重放与洪泛；MCP 服务器能承受格式错误的消息；`max_per_hour` 统计消息；设置在锁下保存；保存的令牌只交给 `gh`；`--doctor` 警告危险的组合；干净安装测试成为发布检查的独立阶段。
精简版与演示的隔离测试、更新检查关闭或离线安装时完全不发网络请求、以选择启动器开头的 README、`--doctor --json`、网络模式的常驻提示条、帮助及其文档的八种语言,以及可选功能(网络模式、监视器保存的令牌、对 GitHub 的操作、`act`、构件的本地副本、自托管运行器、OpenTelemetry、按作业标签的 FinOps);见更新日志和 `ADVANCED.md`。

1.6.4 没有做到的,以及原因:

- **已决定，但 1.6.5 未完成**（本版本限定于完整性与安全）：对外部 AI 的主动通知（默认关闭，每个提供商首次确认，仅封闭列表中已过滤的字段，每小时调用次数与费用上限，通过环境变量名提供密钥，AI 从不执行操作）及其外发命令变体（封闭列表，无 shell）；新的截图（`tools/make_screenshots.py --web` 在发布机器上没有产出，因此手动截取：启动 `--demo`，打开页面，每个标签页保存一张截图）；以及在一个页面中显示多个所有者的仓库。
- **一个页面里多个所有者**:监视器仅凭名称识别仓库(运行、哨兵、缓存、导出),两个所有者若有同名仓库会混在一起。组织会被列出,每个由各自的监视器监视(`github_owner`)。在一个页面中实现需要在每个标识符中加入所有者。
- **用能读取账单报告的登录验证**:没有 `user` 权限范围的登录得到的真实答复是“未找到”,监视器退回估算(已验证);数字本身尚未与账单账户对照。
- **`quotas.json` 中大型运行器的价格**来自对公开价目表的记忆,标记为未验证;请与 GitHub 账单页面比对并编辑该文件。
- **`gh copilot`**:其参数用 `gh copilot -- --help` 检查,这需要 Copilot 命令行;此处未安装,因此仍未验证。
- **通知、webhook、Enterprise Server 和服务示例**对真实服务的验证:`tools/manual_check_live.py` 可手动检查;它们需要你的渠道和主机,所以没有在此运行。
- **终端应用**可编辑简单设置并显示 AI 状态;单个红色工作流的解释以及列表和映射的编辑仍在页面中。
- **会下载或安装的新版本检查**:永不;监视器只会提示。

- **更多通知适配器**:ntfy、Microsoft Teams,以及经本地中继的电子邮件。
- **一个页面里多个账户**:目前每个账户由各自的监视器运行。
- **通过代理获取运行器的硬件遥测**:目前只读取可选的 node exporter 端点。

- 页面登录界面,使网络模式不必输入一次访问令牌。目前的答案是访问令牌,面向互联网则使用带认证的反向代理(见 `monitor/docs/DEPLOYMENT.md`)。
- 在页面中读取失败步骤的日志,并采用与 AI 助手相同的清理方式。
pt:
# Roteiro

Ideias que não couberam na versão atual, sem ordem prometida. São direções, não compromissos; uma issue ou um pull request é a melhor forma de fazer avançar uma.

Uma versão de integridade e segurança, sem grandes funcionalidades novas: um commit verde exige o workflow obrigatório do repositório, um fetch falhado pára o despacho, o catálogo não pode indicar uma ferramenta fora da pasta das ferramentas nem alterar `dry_run`/`ref`, e um lote sem verificação de commit registada deixa de ser oferecido para assinatura; o `act` fica dentro do espaço de trabalho e o Stop termina toda a árvore de processos e os contentores da execução; o modo de rede pode servir HTTPS, bloqueia tokens errados e só aceita IPv4; o webhook recusa repetições e inundações; o servidor MCP sobrevive a mensagens mal formadas; `max_per_hour` conta mensagens; as definições são guardadas sob bloqueio; o token guardado chega só ao `gh`; o `--doctor` avisa de combinações perigosas; o teste de instalação limpa é uma etapa própria do controlo de publicação.

Testes de isolamento da edição lite e da demonstração, nenhum pedido de rede quando a verificação de versão está desligada ou a instalação está isolada, um README que começa pela escolha do lançador, `--doctor --json`, uma barra persistente para o modo rede, a Ajuda e os seus documentos em oito idiomas, e as funções opcionais (modo rede, um token guardado pelo monitor, ações no GitHub, `act`, cópia local de artefactos, runners próprios, OpenTelemetry, FinOps por etiquetas de job); veja o registo de alterações e `ADVANCED.md`.

O que a 1.6.4 não alcançou, e porquê:

- **Decidido, não feito na 1.6.5** (a versão está limitada a integridade e segurança): o aviso ativo a uma IA externa (desligado por omissão, uma primeira confirmação por fornecedor, só os campos já filtrados da lista fechada, um limite de chamadas e de custo por hora, a chave pelo nome de uma variável de ambiente, e a IA nunca executa uma ação) com a sua variante de comando de saída (lista fechada, sem shell); capturas novas (`tools/make_screenshots.py --web` não produziu saída na máquina da publicação, por isso fazem-se à mão: arranque `--demo`, abra a página e guarde uma captura por separador); e os repositórios de vários proprietários numa só página.
- **Vários proprietários numa página**: o monitor identifica um repositório apenas pelo nome (execuções, sentinela, cache, exportações), pelo que dois proprietários com um repositório do mesmo nome se misturariam. As organizações são listadas e cada uma é vigiada pelo seu próprio monitor (`github_owner`). Fazê-lo numa página exige o proprietário em cada identificador.
- **O relatório de faturação com um login que o possa ler**: a resposta real de um login sem o âmbito `user` é «não encontrado» e o monitor volta à estimativa (verificado); os valores em si não foram comparados com uma conta de faturação.
- **Os preços dos runners grandes** em `quotas.json` vêm da memória da tabela pública de preços e estão marcados como não verificados; compare-os com a página de faturação do GitHub e edite o ficheiro.
- **`gh copilot`**: as suas opções verificam-se com `gh copilot -- --help`, que precisa da linha de comandos do Copilot; aqui não está instalada, por isso continuam por verificar.
- **Notificações, webhook, Enterprise Server e exemplos de serviço** contra serviços reais: `tools/manual_check_live.py` verifica-os à mão; precisam dos seus canais e máquinas, por isso não foram executados aqui.
- **A aplicação de terminal** edita as definições simples e mostra o estado da IA; a explicação de um workflow vermelho concreto e a edição de listas e mapas ficam na página.
- **Uma verificação de nova versão que descarregue ou instale**: nunca; o monitor apenas avisa.

- **Mais adaptadores de notificação**: ntfy, Microsoft Teams e e-mail através de um relé local.
- **Várias contas numa página**: hoje cada conta corre no seu próprio monitor.
- **Telemetria de hardware dos runners** através de um agente: hoje só se lê um endpoint opcional de node exporter.
Ideias que precisam primeiro de uma decisão

- Um ecrã de início de sessão para a página, para que o modo rede não exija escrever uma vez o token de acesso. Hoje a resposta é o token de acesso e, para a Internet, um proxy inverso com autenticação (veja `monitor/docs/DEPLOYMENT.md`).
- Ler na página os registos de um passo falhado, com a mesma limpeza que o assistente de IA aplica.

title.ja: 変更履歴

en:
# Changelog

Version of the tool itself (monitor + sentinel + batch tools), semver of its own. The number lives in `tool_version.py`
and is shown as `tool_version` in the sentinel snapshot and by `read_report.py --version`; `make_release.py` refuses to build
when this file and `tool_version.py` disagree.

A release of integrity and security: no large new feature. What cannot be proven is no longer taken as safe.

### Added

- New settings, all with a conservative default: `dispatch.required_ci` (and, in the file, `dispatch.required_ci_repos` and `dispatch.required_ci_profiles`), `act.allow_symlinks`, `listen.tls_cert_file`, `listen.tls_key_file`, `listen.secure_cookie`, `listen.max_failed_attempts`, `webhook.replay_seconds`, `webhook.max_per_minute`; the guide of the settings is regenerated.
- `finalize --accept-legacy` for batches written by an older version, and the `--doctor` checks `risks` and `backend` (eight languages).
- Tests for every change of this release (the suite grew from 729 to more than 800).

### Security

- **A green commit needs the required CI.** `gha_dispatch_all.py` marks a commit green only when the required workflow files succeeded on it (`ci.yml` by default; `dispatch.required_ci`, `dispatch.required_ci_repos`, `dispatch.required_ci_profiles`), nothing failed, timed out or waits for an approval (`action_required` blocks like a failure), nothing is still running and the list of runs is complete (it reads up to five pages; a longer list is not green).
- **A failed `git fetch` stops the dispatch** of that repository, git commands have a time limit and the commit ids are checked; an old `origin/main` is never taken as proof.
- **The catalogue cannot leave its folder or change the dispatch.** `tool` must be a plain file name that sits in the tools folder (links that leave it are refused too); `extra` may only hold `-f key=value` workflow inputs (never `dry_run`, `ref`, `-R`, `--ref`); `finalize_flags` only long flags; the arguments of `gh workflow run` are built from the validated pieces and checked again when the batch fires.
- **Old batches are not signed blindly.** `finalize` offers for signing only a run whose batch recorded that it was built on the commit that was checked. A batch written by an older version is `needs_review`; `finalize --accept-legacy` reads the run again from GitHub, accepts it only if its commit is the recorded one, warns, and asks for the word LEGACY before each signature.
- **`act` stays inside the workspace.** The clone is resolved and must be a real folder of the workspace (a link, a `..` name or a `.github` that points elsewhere is refused; `act.allow_symlinks` allows a link to a clone). The time limit and Stop end the whole tree of processes the run started (a process group on Linux and macOS, `taskkill /T` on its own PID on Windows) and remove the `act-` containers that run created.
- **Network mode**: HTTPS served directly with your own certificate and key (`listen.tls_cert_file`, `listen.tls_key_file`; TLS 1.2 or newer; the monitor does not start on plain HTTP if they cannot be used) or the `Secure` cookie behind an HTTPS proxy (`listen.secure_cookie`); the access token leaves the address bar at once (redirect, no `Referer`); an address that sends too many wrong tokens is refused for five minutes (`listen.max_failed_attempts`); the address of the page is the one the server listens on; only IPv4 addresses are accepted, in the settings and in the guard alike; the console says when the connection is plain HTTP.
- **Webhook**: every delivery needs its `X-GitHub-Delivery` id and a repeated one is ignored for `webhook.replay_seconds`; a repository can cause at most `webhook.max_per_minute` accepted events a minute; the owner in `full_name` must be the watched account; one address is limited to 120 requests a minute in the network mode; an accepted event drops the stored conditional reads of that repository and marks it for the next cycle; a signature header with unusual characters is a plain refusal.
- **MCP server**: a message of the wrong shape (parameters, arguments, id, method) gets an error for that message only, an unexpected defect in a tool is an internal error that does not end the server, and a line over 64 KB is refused.
- **The stored GitHub token is given to `gh` only.** It is no longer put in the environment of the monitor, so `act`, your notification command and every other child cannot inherit it.
- **A GET never writes.** The copy of the daily report in the audit folder is a POST with the one-use token (`/api/sentinel/parte/save`); `?save=1` on the GET is gone.
- `--doctor` names dangerous combinations (network mode on every interface, AI actions that execute while the network mode is on, `act` while the network mode is on, the token in a plain file) and shows where the token is kept, never the token.

### Fixed

- `max_per_hour` of the notifications now limits messages (one unit per channel, booked at once under one lock) and not events; a channel that cannot send books nothing.
- Two saves of the settings at the same time no longer lose one of them (a lock in the process and a lock file).
- The signing queue export says why it did not write (a refused drive or network path, a folder instead of a file, the error of the system) instead of a bare refusal.
- The secondary-limit wait and the retry after a timeout carry a random jitter.
- The test that unpacks the zip in a clean folder is no longer part of the ordinary suite: `make_release.py` runs the suite once with a time limit, then the clean install as its own stage, and shows stdout and stderr when either fails.

### Changed

- The guides of notifications, webhook, advanced features, outputs, AI alerts and migration say all of this in the eight languages; `docs/MIGRATING.md` has a block from 1.6.4 to 1.6.5.

### Added

- **Alerts for AIs**: the monitor writes a local, read-only feed (`ai_alerts.jsonl`, one line per event, and `ALERTS_BRIEF.md`, rewritten at every cycle, 2 KB by default) with one alert per red workflow: stable id, severity, probable cause told apart as real or transient with editable rules, suggested action, and a state (open, acknowledged, resolved by itself when the workflow turns green). Everything goes through a cleaner of tokens, keys, e-mail addresses, IP addresses and home folders. `GET /api/ai/brief` and `GET /api/ai/alerts`, an optional read-only MCP server (`mcp_server.py`: `get_alerts`, `get_red_repos`, `get_run_failure`, `get_quota`, and `ack_alert` with `--allow-ack`), a notification when a new REAL alert appears, an optional hook to an address on this computer (off), and an optional `ai_hint` in `ci_red.json`. New guide `AI_ALERTS.md` in eight languages.
- **Opt-in features, all off by default, each with its switch in Settings > Advanced** and tests that prove they refuse without the switch, the confirmation or the token: the network mode (a private address, an access token for every request, accepted host names, a persistent red bar, exposure keys changeable only from the computer itself); a GitHub token kept by the monitor in the secure store of the system (Windows DPAPI, macOS Keychain, Linux Secret Service, else a file with permissions 600) and never in a setting, a log or an answer, with a delete button; actions on GitHub (run again, cancel, close, merge), each confirmed on its own after showing exactly what will be sent; running a workflow here with `act` from a closed list, with no real secrets; a local mirror of artifacts; self-hosted runners (idle, busy, offline, optional disk and load); OpenTelemetry export (traces and metrics, OTLP/HTTP JSON); the organisations of the login; FinOps by job labels (Linux, Windows, macOS and larger runners), the price of the minutes above the included ones, Codespaces, Packages and storage from the billing report. New guide `ADVANCED.md` in eight languages, and `tools/manual_check_live.py` to try the real services by hand.
- `--doctor --json`; the doctor also reports busy ports, the allowance left, whether you have your own targets file, the one-use token and the exposure. The README of the package starts with the choice of launcher (complete, lite, batch, terminal, doctor, demo).
- The terminal application edits the simple settings (not the security ones) and has an AI tab; a persistent banner for settings that need a restart survives a reload; the header shows when the sentinel's A10 is paused for quota and how much of the minutes budget is used; the welcome is remembered by the server too.
- `redrule.py` ignores the dynamic runs of dependency updates like the dashboard does, and the shared cases of the rule are now a test fixture.

### Changed

- **The Help is complete in eight languages**: the roadmap, contributing, security and support documents are translated, the fixed labels of the changelog are translated and its entries are marked as English only, with a translated notice; `tools/make_help_index.py --check` and a test fail when a topic lacks a language. A search shows at most 30 hits and a huge document no longer holds the server thread.
- The red tile counts workflows in both editions and says in how many repositories. The lite edition inherits the refresh rhythm of the complete one at its first start.
- A passing failure (a TLS hiccup, a 5xx) is retried with an exponential backoff and is shown as an error only after three cycles in a row; the last picture stays.
- The terminal view of the lite edition no longer asks for the sentinel; the lite edition never loads the sentinel module (the local guard moved to `localguard.py`).
- `--demo` redirects every file it could write (logs, caches, event feed, history, welcome) to its temporary folder.

### Security

- With `updates.check` off or `airgapped` on, the monitor makes no network request at all for the update notice (tested).
- Verified against the real GitHub API: the scopes of the token are read correctly, the organisations list and the billing report degrade silently (a login without the `user` scope gets "not found" and the monitor keeps the estimate).

### Added

- **About panel** (the **i** button of the header, in both editions): version, edition, author, licence, Python and system, links (repository, releases, changelog, documentation, issues), the files it uses (read only), the health of the server, the credits of the libraries and a button that copies the information for support (no secret, no token, the home folder shown as `~`). `GET /api/about`, and `--about` in the console.
- **Help panel** (the **?** button, the key `?`, and a "?" in the tab bar that opens the page of the tab you are on): the whole documentation (README, quick start, every guide, roadmap, changelog, contributing, security) as an index you can search, in the language of the page and in English where a document is not translated, served by the local server without Internet. It is built from the real documents by `tools/make_help_index.py` (`--check` in the CI), so no text is written twice; the markdown is rendered safely (everything escaped, no image loaded, only `http(s)` links and links to other documents). In the console: `--help-topics [TOPIC]` and `--help-search WORDS`.
- **Notice of a newer version**: a discreet badge in the header, a line in About, in the console and in `--doctor` when a newer release is published. One read-only request a day to the public releases page, through the same client as everything else (conditional read), never downloads or installs anything, sends nothing about you, ignores pre-releases, compares versions as numbers (1.6.10 is newer than 1.6.9), is silent offline and is off with `updates.check` or in an air-gapped installation (`airgapped`).
- **Settings > Basic**, the first tab: open the browser at start, the update notice, the air-gapped switch, the one-use token, the discovery options, the lifecycle rules, and the plan and quotas. Under it, what the monitor found in the account (owner, repositories found, watched, left out), the news and the suggested groups.
- **`--doctor`**: Python, `gh`, the login, the allowance, the network, the write permission of the folder, a free port, and the optional Docker, Rich and Textual; each failure comes with the exact command that fixes it, in eight languages.

A release of integrity and security: no large new feature. What cannot be proven is no longer taken as safe.

### Añadido
- New settings, all with a conservative default: `dispatch.required_ci` (and, in the file, `dispatch.required_ci_repos` and `dispatch.required_ci_profiles`), `act.allow_symlinks`, `listen.tls_cert_file`, `listen.tls_key_file`, `listen.secure_cookie`, `listen.max_failed_attempts`, `webhook.replay_seconds`, `webhook.max_per_minute`; the guide of the settings is regenerated.
- `finalize --accept-legacy` for batches written by an older version, and the `--doctor` checks `risks` and `backend` (eight languages).
- Tests for every change of this release (the suite grew from 729 to more than 800).

### Seguridad
- **A green commit needs the required CI.** `gha_dispatch_all.py` marks a commit green only when the required workflow files succeeded on it (`ci.yml` by default; `dispatch.required_ci`, `dispatch.required_ci_repos`, `dispatch.required_ci_profiles`), nothing failed, timed out or waits for an approval (`action_required` blocks like a failure), nothing is still running and the list of runs is complete (it reads up to five pages; a longer list is not green).
- **A failed `git fetch` stops the dispatch** of that repository, git commands have a time limit and the commit ids are checked; an old `origin/main` is never taken as proof.
- **The catalogue cannot leave its folder or change the dispatch.** `tool` must be a plain file name that sits in the tools folder (links that leave it are refused too); `extra` may only hold `-f key=value` workflow inputs (never `dry_run`, `ref`, `-R`, `--ref`); `finalize_flags` only long flags; the arguments of `gh workflow run` are built from the validated pieces and checked again when the batch fires.
- **Old batches are not signed blindly.** `finalize` offers for signing only a run whose batch recorded that it was built on the commit that was checked. A batch written by an older version is `needs_review`; `finalize --accept-legacy` reads the run again from GitHub, accepts it only if its commit is the recorded one, warns, and asks for the word LEGACY before each signature.
- **`act` stays inside the workspace.** The clone is resolved and must be a real folder of the workspace (a link, a `..` name or a `.github` that points elsewhere is refused; `act.allow_symlinks` allows a link to a clone). The time limit and Stop end the whole tree of processes the run started (a process group on Linux and macOS, `taskkill /T` on its own PID on Windows) and remove the `act-` containers that run created.
- **Network mode**: HTTPS served directly with your own certificate and key (`listen.tls_cert_file`, `listen.tls_key_file`; TLS 1.2 or newer; the monitor does not start on plain HTTP if they cannot be used) or the `Secure` cookie behind an HTTPS proxy (`listen.secure_cookie`); the access token leaves the address bar at once (redirect, no `Referer`); an address that sends too many wrong tokens is refused for five minutes (`listen.max_failed_attempts`); the address of the page is the one the server listens on; only IPv4 addresses are accepted, in the settings and in the guard alike; the console says when the connection is plain HTTP.
- **Webhook**: every delivery needs its `X-GitHub-Delivery` id and a repeated one is ignored for `webhook.replay_seconds`; a repository can cause at most `webhook.max_per_minute` accepted events a minute; the owner in `full_name` must be the watched account; one address is limited to 120 requests a minute in the network mode; an accepted event drops the stored conditional reads of that repository and marks it for the next cycle; a signature header with unusual characters is a plain refusal.
- **MCP server**: a message of the wrong shape (parameters, arguments, id, method) gets an error for that message only, an unexpected defect in a tool is an internal error that does not end the server, and a line over 64 KB is refused.
- **The stored GitHub token is given to `gh` only.** It is no longer put in the environment of the monitor, so `act`, your notification command and every other child cannot inherit it.
- **A GET never writes.** The copy of the daily report in the audit folder is a POST with the one-use token (`/api/sentinel/parte/save`); `?save=1` on the GET is gone.
- `--doctor` names dangerous combinations (network mode on every interface, AI actions that execute while the network mode is on, `act` while the network mode is on, the token in a plain file) and shows where the token is kept, never the token.

### Corregido
- `max_per_hour` of the notifications now limits messages (one unit per channel, booked at once under one lock) and not events; a channel that cannot send books nothing.
- Two saves of the settings at the same time no longer lose one of them (a lock in the process and a lock file).
- The signing queue export says why it did not write (a refused drive or network path, a folder instead of a file, the error of the system) instead of a bare refusal.
- The secondary-limit wait and the retry after a timeout carry a random jitter.
- The test that unpacks the zip in a clean folder is no longer part of the ordinary suite: `make_release.py` runs the suite once with a time limit, then the clean install as its own stage, and shows stdout and stderr when either fails.

A release of integrity and security: no large new feature. What cannot be proven is no longer taken as safe.

### Hinzugefügt
- New settings, all with a conservative default: `dispatch.required_ci` (and, in the file, `dispatch.required_ci_repos` and `dispatch.required_ci_profiles`), `act.allow_symlinks`, `listen.tls_cert_file`, `listen.tls_key_file`, `listen.secure_cookie`, `listen.max_failed_attempts`, `webhook.replay_seconds`, `webhook.max_per_minute`; the guide of the settings is regenerated.
- `finalize --accept-legacy` for batches written by an older version, and the `--doctor` checks `risks` and `backend` (eight languages).
- Tests for every change of this release (the suite grew from 729 to more than 800).

### Sicherheit
- **A green commit needs the required CI.** `gha_dispatch_all.py` marks a commit green only when the required workflow files succeeded on it (`ci.yml` by default; `dispatch.required_ci`, `dispatch.required_ci_repos`, `dispatch.required_ci_profiles`), nothing failed, timed out or waits for an approval (`action_required` blocks like a failure), nothing is still running and the list of runs is complete (it reads up to five pages; a longer list is not green).
- **A failed `git fetch` stops the dispatch** of that repository, git commands have a time limit and the commit ids are checked; an old `origin/main` is never taken as proof.
- **The catalogue cannot leave its folder or change the dispatch.** `tool` must be a plain file name that sits in the tools folder (links that leave it are refused too); `extra` may only hold `-f key=value` workflow inputs (never `dry_run`, `ref`, `-R`, `--ref`); `finalize_flags` only long flags; the arguments of `gh workflow run` are built from the validated pieces and checked again when the batch fires.
- **Old batches are not signed blindly.** `finalize` offers for signing only a run whose batch recorded that it was built on the commit that was checked. A batch written by an older version is `needs_review`; `finalize --accept-legacy` reads the run again from GitHub, accepts it only if its commit is the recorded one, warns, and asks for the word LEGACY before each signature.
- **`act` stays inside the workspace.** The clone is resolved and must be a real folder of the workspace (a link, a `..` name or a `.github` that points elsewhere is refused; `act.allow_symlinks` allows a link to a clone). The time limit and Stop end the whole tree of processes the run started (a process group on Linux and macOS, `taskkill /T` on its own PID on Windows) and remove the `act-` containers that run created.
- **Network mode**: HTTPS served directly with your own certificate and key (`listen.tls_cert_file`, `listen.tls_key_file`; TLS 1.2 or newer; the monitor does not start on plain HTTP if they cannot be used) or the `Secure` cookie behind an HTTPS proxy (`listen.secure_cookie`); the access token leaves the address bar at once (redirect, no `Referer`); an address that sends too many wrong tokens is refused for five minutes (`listen.max_failed_attempts`); the address of the page is the one the server listens on; only IPv4 addresses are accepted, in the settings and in the guard alike; the console says when the connection is plain HTTP.
- **Webhook**: every delivery needs its `X-GitHub-Delivery` id and a repeated one is ignored for `webhook.replay_seconds`; a repository can cause at most `webhook.max_per_minute` accepted events a minute; the owner in `full_name` must be the watched account; one address is limited to 120 requests a minute in the network mode; an accepted event drops the stored conditional reads of that repository and marks it for the next cycle; a signature header with unusual characters is a plain refusal.
- **MCP server**: a message of the wrong shape (parameters, arguments, id, method) gets an error for that message only, an unexpected defect in a tool is an internal error that does not end the server, and a line over 64 KB is refused.
- **The stored GitHub token is given to `gh` only.** It is no longer put in the environment of the monitor, so `act`, your notification command and every other child cannot inherit it.
- **A GET never writes.** The copy of the daily report in the audit folder is a POST with the one-use token (`/api/sentinel/parte/save`); `?save=1` on the GET is gone.
- `--doctor` names dangerous combinations (network mode on every interface, AI actions that execute while the network mode is on, `act` while the network mode is on, the token in a plain file) and shows where the token is kept, never the token.

### Behoben
- `max_per_hour` of the notifications now limits messages (one unit per channel, booked at once under one lock) and not events; a channel that cannot send books nothing.
- Two saves of the settings at the same time no longer lose one of them (a lock in the process and a lock file).
- The signing queue export says why it did not write (a refused drive or network path, a folder instead of a file, the error of the system) instead of a bare refusal.
- The secondary-limit wait and the retry after a timeout carry a random jitter.
- The test that unpacks the zip in a clean folder is no longer part of the ordinary suite: `make_release.py` runs the suite once with a time limit, then the clean install as its own stage, and shows stdout and stderr when either fails.

### Geändert

Everything goes through a cleaner of tokens, keys, e-mail addresses, IP addresses and home folders. `GET /api/ai/brief` and `GET /api/ai/alerts`, an optional read-only MCP server (`mcp_server.py`: `get_alerts`, `get_red_repos`, `get_run_failure`, `get_quota`, and `ack_alert` with `--allow-ack`), a notification when a new REAL alert appears, an optional hook to an address on this computer (off), and an optional `ai_hint` in `ci_red.json`. New guide `AI_ALERTS.md` in eight languages.

  key each ecosystem pins (URTC `release_sign.py`, ARMOR helper `PACKAGE_PUBLIC_KEY`, HYDRA updater `RELEASES_PUBLIC_KEY`, or `sentinel.signature_pubkeys`).
  Every state now carries `signature_kind` (none | dev | release) and `signature_verified` (true | false | "unknown"); only a release signature that verifies
  (`trusted`) lowers the pending-signature alert, besides "published". A signature that does not verify keeps the alert and says so in the report.
  `sentinel.require_verified_signature` (default true; false = the 1.0.0 rule). Formats this module cannot check (.sig2, .hdr2, .imgsig, APK, hydra-sign) are
  "unknown", never "false". The build attestation still needs the network and stays with the signing tools.
- `ci_red.json` schema 2: per repository a `pending_sign` list (workflow, hours, state, signature_kind, signature_verified, last_build_at, url) next to the red
  workflows, plus `schema`, `pending_sign_repos` and the threshold; the format is documented in `ci_red.py` and is only ever extended.
- One definition of "last run on main" (`signstate.completed_runs`) shared by the red check, the green-without-release check and the target states.
- `ci_red.target_path` refuses D: paths, WSL/Git Bash forms of D: and drive/UNC paths that the running system cannot use; the tests simulate both systems
  and the whole suite now passes on Linux.
- `gha_dispatch_all.py plan` always ends with the section "Signature orphans" (green CI + known `*-build.yml` + no target); coverage is by repository AND workflow.
- Convention for targets (ecosystem prefix -> default signing tool, workflow in the known list); `targets.json` only holds the overrides and always wins.
  `hygiene --write-candidates` writes the proposed entries to `targets.candidates.json` (never applied by itself, never packaged).
- Page: clickable header counters "red on main" and "unsigned" (filter the repositories; the second one also focuses the signing queue), the signing queue
  with its commands and a copy button, repository panel with build / signed / published, signature kind and verification, and the suggested command;
  a header badge when a minutes budget reaches 80 % (red when exceeded); "yesterday vs today" also compares budget warnings and the lines of the report.

Not done: reading the build attestation / SBOM (network); `HYDRA-UMC-OS` has a build workflow but its signing tool does not support it yet (listed as an orphan).

First numbered version. What the package does:

- Monitor of GitHub Actions for the four ecosystems (local web page, run cache, stuck builds, build-failed/build-stuck issues).
- Sentinel layer A (read only, no AI needed): A1 stuck builds, A2 red CI (one criterion: last completed run of each workflow on the default
  branch), A3 CodeQL/Dependabot/secret alerts, A4 Dependabot pull requests, A5 releases (candidates, green builds without a release,
  pending signature), A6 hygiene, A7 consumption (minutes and API allowance), A8 audits and rounds, A9 roadmap boards.
- Explicit state of each build target: built_on_gha -> signed_local (none | dev | release) -> published, with `last_build_at`,
  `last_signed_at`, `signature_kind` and the real hours waiting; local batch and signed-folder records lower the pending-signature
  alert without waiting for GitHub.
- Signing queue of the day (`a5.sign_queue`): most urgent first, with the exact finalize command of each target.
- Budget of Actions minutes per ecosystem (`sentinel.minutes_budget`, empty by default): warning at 80 % in the report and as an event.
- Event feed (`events_monitor.jsonl`) and `ci_red.json` (repository -> red workflows + hours pending signature), written atomically.
- Batch tools: `gha_dispatch_all.py plan|dispatch|status|finalize|hygiene` with `--only` or `--ecosystem`, `plan --json`,
  `finalize --json`, one retry of a failed dispatch at the end of the batch, targets as data in `targets.json`.
- `read_report.py`: the report as plain text from the running monitor, without spending API quota.
- `make_release.py`: quality gate (unit tests, clean zip, complete example configuration, version/changelog agreement) and SHA256SUMS.

Not done in this version: verifying release signatures against the public key and the build attestation from the sentinel
(different signature formats per ecosystem; the attestation needs the network; the signing tools verify both before publishing).

# Journal des modifications
Version of the tool itself (monitor + sentinel + batch tools), semver of its own. The number lives in `tool_version.py`
and is shown as `tool_version` in the sentinel snapshot and by `read_report.py --version`; `make_release.py` refuses to build
when this file and `tool_version.py` disagree.

A release of integrity and security: no large new feature. What cannot be proven is no longer taken as safe.

### Ajouté
- New settings, all with a conservative default: `dispatch.required_ci` (and, in the file, `dispatch.required_ci_repos` and `dispatch.required_ci_profiles`), `act.allow_symlinks`, `listen.tls_cert_file`, `listen.tls_key_file`, `listen.secure_cookie`, `listen.max_failed_attempts`, `webhook.replay_seconds`, `webhook.max_per_minute`; the guide of the settings is regenerated.
- `finalize --accept-legacy` for batches written by an older version, and the `--doctor` checks `risks` and `backend` (eight languages).
- Tests for every change of this release (the suite grew from 729 to more than 800).

### Sécurité
- **A green commit needs the required CI.** `gha_dispatch_all.py` marks a commit green only when the required workflow files succeeded on it (`ci.yml` by default; `dispatch.required_ci`, `dispatch.required_ci_repos`, `dispatch.required_ci_profiles`), nothing failed, timed out or waits for an approval (`action_required` blocks like a failure), nothing is still running and the list of runs is complete (it reads up to five pages; a longer list is not green).
- **A failed `git fetch` stops the dispatch** of that repository, git commands have a time limit and the commit ids are checked; an old `origin/main` is never taken as proof.
- **The catalogue cannot leave its folder or change the dispatch.** `tool` must be a plain file name that sits in the tools folder (links that leave it are refused too); `extra` may only hold `-f key=value` workflow inputs (never `dry_run`, `ref`, `-R`, `--ref`); `finalize_flags` only long flags; the arguments of `gh workflow run` are built from the validated pieces and checked again when the batch fires.
- **Old batches are not signed blindly.** `finalize` offers for signing only a run whose batch recorded that it was built on the commit that was checked. A batch written by an older version is `needs_review`; `finalize --accept-legacy` reads the run again from GitHub, accepts it only if its commit is the recorded one, warns, and asks for the word LEGACY before each signature.
- **`act` stays inside the workspace.** The clone is resolved and must be a real folder of the workspace (a link, a `..` name or a `.github` that points elsewhere is refused; `act.allow_symlinks` allows a link to a clone). The time limit and Stop end the whole tree of processes the run started (a process group on Linux and macOS, `taskkill /T` on its own PID on Windows) and remove the `act-` containers that run created.
- **Network mode**: HTTPS served directly with your own certificate and key (`listen.tls_cert_file`, `listen.tls_key_file`; TLS 1.2 or newer; the monitor does not start on plain HTTP if they cannot be used) or the `Secure` cookie behind an HTTPS proxy (`listen.secure_cookie`); the access token leaves the address bar at once (redirect, no `Referer`); an address that sends too many wrong tokens is refused for five minutes (`listen.max_failed_attempts`); the address of the page is the one the server listens on; only IPv4 addresses are accepted, in the settings and in the guard alike; the console says when the connection is plain HTTP.
- **Webhook**: every delivery needs its `X-GitHub-Delivery` id and a repeated one is ignored for `webhook.replay_seconds`; a repository can cause at most `webhook.max_per_minute` accepted events a minute; the owner in `full_name` must be the watched account; one address is limited to 120 requests a minute in the network mode; an accepted event drops the stored conditional reads of that repository and marks it for the next cycle; a signature header with unusual characters is a plain refusal.
- **MCP server**: a message of the wrong shape (parameters, arguments, id, method) gets an error for that message only, an unexpected defect in a tool is an internal error that does not end the server, and a line over 64 KB is refused.
- **The stored GitHub token is given to `gh` only.** It is no longer put in the environment of the monitor, so `act`, your notification command and every other child cannot inherit it.
- **A GET never writes.** The copy of the daily report in the audit folder is a POST with the one-use token (`/api/sentinel/parte/save`); `?save=1` on the GET is gone.
- `--doctor` names dangerous combinations (network mode on every interface, AI actions that execute while the network mode is on, `act` while the network mode is on, the token in a plain file) and shows where the token is kept, never the token.

### Corrigé
- `max_per_hour` of the notifications now limits messages (one unit per channel, booked at once under one lock) and not events; a channel that cannot send books nothing.
- Two saves of the settings at the same time no longer lose one of them (a lock in the process and a lock file).
- The signing queue export says why it did not write (a refused drive or network path, a folder instead of a file, the error of the system) instead of a bare refusal.
- The secondary-limit wait and the retry after a timeout carry a random jitter.
- The test that unpacks the zip in a clean folder is no longer part of the ordinary suite: `make_release.py` runs the suite once with a time limit, then the clean install as its own stage, and shows stdout and stderr when either fails.

### Modifié
- The guides of notifications, webhook, advanced features, outputs, AI alerts and migration say all of this in the eight languages; `docs/MIGRATING.md` has a block from 1.6.4 to 1.6.5.

### Ajouté
- **Alerts for AIs**: the monitor writes a local, read-only feed (`ai_alerts.jsonl`, one line per event, and `ALERTS_BRIEF.md`, rewritten at every cycle, 2 KB by default) with one alert per red workflow: stable id, severity, probable cause told apart as real or transient with editable rules, suggested action, and a state (open, acknowledged, resolved by itself when the workflow turns green). Everything goes through a cleaner of tokens, keys, e-mail addresses, IP addresses and home folders. `GET /api/ai/brief` and `GET /api/ai/alerts`, an optional read-only MCP server (`mcp_server.py`: `get_alerts`, `get_red_repos`, `get_run_failure`, `get_quota`, and `ack_alert` with `--allow-ack`), a notification when a new REAL alert appears, an optional hook to an address on this computer (off), and an optional `ai_hint` in `ci_red.json`. New guide `AI_ALERTS.md` in eight languages.
- **Opt-in features, all off by default, each with its switch in Settings > Advanced** and tests that prove they refuse without the switch, the confirmation or the token: the network mode (a private address, an access token for every request, accepted host names, a persistent red bar, exposure keys changeable only from the computer itself); a GitHub token kept by the monitor in the secure store of the system (Windows DPAPI, macOS Keychain, Linux Secret Service, else a file with permissions 600) and never in a setting, a log or an answer, with a delete button; actions on GitHub (run again, cancel, close, merge), each confirmed on its own after showing exactly what will be sent; running a workflow here with `act` from a closed list, with no real secrets; a local mirror of artifacts; self-hosted runners (idle, busy, offline, optional disk and load); OpenTelemetry export (traces and metrics, OTLP/HTTP JSON); the organisations of the login; FinOps by job labels (Linux, Windows, macOS and larger runners), the price of the minutes above the included ones, Codespaces, Packages and storage from the billing report. New guide `ADVANCED.md` in eight languages, and `tools/manual_check_live.py` to try the real services by hand.
- `--doctor --json`; the doctor also reports busy ports, the allowance left, whether you have your own targets file, the one-use token and the exposure. The README of the package starts with the choice of launcher (complete, lite, batch, terminal, doctor, demo).
- The terminal application edits the simple settings (not the security ones) and has an AI tab; a persistent banner for settings that need a restart survives a reload; the header shows when the sentinel's A10 is paused for quota and how much of the minutes budget is used; the welcome is remembered by the server too.
- `redrule.py` ignores the dynamic runs of dependency updates like the dashboard does, and the shared cases of the rule are now a test fixture.

### Modifié
- **The Help is complete in eight languages**: the roadmap, contributing, security and support documents are translated, the fixed labels of the changelog are translated and its entries are marked as English only, with a translated notice; `tools/make_help_index.py --check` and a test fail when a topic lacks a language. A search shows at most 30 hits and a huge document no longer holds the server thread.

- A passing failure (a TLS hiccup, a 5xx) is retried with an exponential backoff and is shown as an error only after three cycles in a row; the last picture stays.
- The terminal view of the lite edition no longer asks for the sentinel; the lite edition never loads the sentinel module (the local guard moved to `localguard.py`).
- `--demo` redirects every file it could write (logs, caches, event feed, history, welcome) to its temporary folder.

### Sécurité

### Ajouté
- **About panel** (the **i** button of the header, in both editions): version, edition, author, licence, Python and system, links (repository, releases, changelog, documentation, issues), the files it uses (read only), the health of the server, the credits of the libraries and a button that copies the information for support (no secret, no token, the home folder shown as `~`). `GET /api/about`, and `--about` in the console.

It is built from the real documents by `tools/make_help_index.py` (`--check` in the CI), so no text is written twice; the markdown is rendered safely (everything escaped, no image loaded, only `http(s)` links and links to other documents). In the console: `--help-topics [TOPIC]` and `--help-search WORDS`.

The simple Rich view (`tui.py`, `--once`) stays and also has `--about` and `--help-topics`.

### Sécurité

### Ajouté

### Ajouté

### Modifié

# Registro delle modifiche
Version of the tool itself (monitor + sentinel + batch tools), semver of its own. The number lives in `tool_version.py`
and is shown as `tool_version` in the sentinel snapshot and by `read_report.py --version`; `make_release.py` refuses to build
when this file and `tool_version.py` disagree.

A release of integrity and security: no large new feature. What cannot be proven is no longer taken as safe.

### Aggiunto
- New settings, all with a conservative default: `dispatch.required_ci` (and, in the file, `dispatch.required_ci_repos` and `dispatch.required_ci_profiles`), `act.allow_symlinks`, `listen.tls_cert_file`, `listen.tls_key_file`, `listen.secure_cookie`, `listen.max_failed_attempts`, `webhook.replay_seconds`, `webhook.max_per_minute`; the guide of the settings is regenerated.
- `finalize --accept-legacy` for batches written by an older version, and the `--doctor` checks `risks` and `backend` (eight languages).
- Tests for every change of this release (the suite grew from 729 to more than 800).

### Sicurezza
- **A green commit needs the required CI.** `gha_dispatch_all.py` marks a commit green only when the required workflow files succeeded on it (`ci.yml` by default; `dispatch.required_ci`, `dispatch.required_ci_repos`, `dispatch.required_ci_profiles`), nothing failed, timed out or waits for an approval (`action_required` blocks like a failure), nothing is still running and the list of runs is complete (it reads up to five pages; a longer list is not green).
- **A failed `git fetch` stops the dispatch** of that repository, git commands have a time limit and the commit ids are checked; an old `origin/main` is never taken as proof.
- **The catalogue cannot leave its folder or change the dispatch.** `tool` must be a plain file name that sits in the tools folder (links that leave it are refused too); `extra` may only hold `-f key=value` workflow inputs (never `dry_run`, `ref`, `-R`, `--ref`); `finalize_flags` only long flags; the arguments of `gh workflow run` are built from the validated pieces and checked again when the batch fires.
- **Old batches are not signed blindly.** `finalize` offers for signing only a run whose batch recorded that it was built on the commit that was checked. A batch written by an older version is `needs_review`; `finalize --accept-legacy` reads the run again from GitHub, accepts it only if its commit is the recorded one, warns, and asks for the word LEGACY before each signature.
- **`act` stays inside the workspace.** The clone is resolved and must be a real folder of the workspace (a link, a `..` name or a `.github` that points elsewhere is refused; `act.allow_symlinks` allows a link to a clone). The time limit and Stop end the whole tree of processes the run started (a process group on Linux and macOS, `taskkill /T` on its own PID on Windows) and remove the `act-` containers that run created.
- **Network mode**: HTTPS served directly with your own certificate and key (`listen.tls_cert_file`, `listen.tls_key_file`; TLS 1.2 or newer; the monitor does not start on plain HTTP if they cannot be used) or the `Secure` cookie behind an HTTPS proxy (`listen.secure_cookie`); the access token leaves the address bar at once (redirect, no `Referer`); an address that sends too many wrong tokens is refused for five minutes (`listen.max_failed_attempts`); the address of the page is the one the server listens on; only IPv4 addresses are accepted, in the settings and in the guard alike; the console says when the connection is plain HTTP.
- **Webhook**: every delivery needs its `X-GitHub-Delivery` id and a repeated one is ignored for `webhook.replay_seconds`; a repository can cause at most `webhook.max_per_minute` accepted events a minute; the owner in `full_name` must be the watched account; one address is limited to 120 requests a minute in the network mode; an accepted event drops the stored conditional reads of that repository and marks it for the next cycle; a signature header with unusual characters is a plain refusal.
- **MCP server**: a message of the wrong shape (parameters, arguments, id, method) gets an error for that message only, an unexpected defect in a tool is an internal error that does not end the server, and a line over 64 KB is refused.
- **The stored GitHub token is given to `gh` only.** It is no longer put in the environment of the monitor, so `act`, your notification command and every other child cannot inherit it.
- **A GET never writes.** The copy of the daily report in the audit folder is a POST with the one-use token (`/api/sentinel/parte/save`); `?save=1` on the GET is gone.
- `--doctor` names dangerous combinations (network mode on every interface, AI actions that execute while the network mode is on, `act` while the network mode is on, the token in a plain file) and shows where the token is kept, never the token.

### Corretto
- `max_per_hour` of the notifications now limits messages (one unit per channel, booked at once under one lock) and not events; a channel that cannot send books nothing.
- Two saves of the settings at the same time no longer lose one of them (a lock in the process and a lock file).
- The signing queue export says why it did not write (a refused drive or network path, a folder instead of a file, the error of the system) instead of a bare refusal.
- The secondary-limit wait and the retry after a timeout carry a random jitter.
- The test that unpacks the zip in a clean folder is no longer part of the ordinary suite: `make_release.py` runs the suite once with a time limit, then the clean install as its own stage, and shows stdout and stderr when either fails.

### Corretto
- **The linter no longer cries wolf on placeholders**: a value that looks like a secret is classified (a known token format or a long high-entropy string is serious, a readable filler such as `placeholder` or `changeme` is only information, anything else a warning; references and empty values are no finding) and its value is never printed or stored.
- **A browser that closes or reloads its tab while the page is loading no longer prints a traceback** (`ConnectionAbortedError`, `ConnectionResetError`, `BrokenPipeError`): they are counted in `ghamon_client_disconnects_total`; a real error is still shown.

### Sicurezza
- The incoming webhook stays off by default, on `127.0.0.1`, with a mandatory HMAC.
- Notification secrets live only in environment variables; hosts are fixed; notifications never write to GitHub.
- AI actions: running one needs its own switch and a confirmation of the full command each time, only on targets the monitor already watches, with a limit per hour, a local log and a lock after two failures in a row.

# 変更履歴
Version of the tool itself (monitor + sentinel + batch tools), semver of its own. The number lives in `tool_version.py`

A release of integrity and security: no large new feature. What cannot be proven is no longer taken as safe.

### 追加
- New settings, all with a conservative default: `dispatch.required_ci` (and, in the file, `dispatch.required_ci_repos` and `dispatch.required_ci_profiles`), `act.allow_symlinks`, `listen.tls_cert_file`, `listen.tls_key_file`, `listen.secure_cookie`, `listen.max_failed_attempts`, `webhook.replay_seconds`, `webhook.max_per_minute`; the guide of the settings is regenerated.
- `finalize --accept-legacy` for batches written by an older version, and the `--doctor` checks `risks` and `backend` (eight languages).
- Tests for every change of this release (the suite grew from 729 to more than 800).

### セキュリティ
- **A green commit needs the required CI.** `gha_dispatch_all.py` marks a commit green only when the required workflow files succeeded on it (`ci.yml` by default; `dispatch.required_ci`, `dispatch.required_ci_repos`, `dispatch.required_ci_profiles`), nothing failed, timed out or waits for an approval (`action_required` blocks like a failure), nothing is still running and the list of runs is complete (it reads up to five pages; a longer list is not green).
- **A failed `git fetch` stops the dispatch** of that repository, git commands have a time limit and the commit ids are checked; an old `origin/main` is never taken as proof.
- **The catalogue cannot leave its folder or change the dispatch.** `tool` must be a plain file name that sits in the tools folder (links that leave it are refused too); `extra` may only hold `-f key=value` workflow inputs (never `dry_run`, `ref`, `-R`, `--ref`); `finalize_flags` only long flags; the arguments of `gh workflow run` are built from the validated pieces and checked again when the batch fires.
- **Old batches are not signed blindly.** `finalize` offers for signing only a run whose batch recorded that it was built on the commit that was checked. A batch written by an older version is `needs_review`; `finalize --accept-legacy` reads the run again from GitHub, accepts it only if its commit is the recorded one, warns, and asks for the word LEGACY before each signature.
- **`act` stays inside the workspace.** The clone is resolved and must be a real folder of the workspace (a link, a `..` name or a `.github` that points elsewhere is refused; `act.allow_symlinks` allows a link to a clone). The time limit and Stop end the whole tree of processes the run started (a process group on Linux and macOS, `taskkill /T` on its own PID on Windows) and remove the `act-` containers that run created.
- **Network mode**: HTTPS served directly with your own certificate and key (`listen.tls_cert_file`, `listen.tls_key_file`; TLS 1.2 or newer; the monitor does not start on plain HTTP if they cannot be used) or the `Secure` cookie behind an HTTPS proxy (`listen.secure_cookie`); the access token leaves the address bar at once (redirect, no `Referer`); an address that sends too many wrong tokens is refused for five minutes (`listen.max_failed_attempts`); the address of the page is the one the server listens on; only IPv4 addresses are accepted, in the settings and in the guard alike; the console says when the connection is plain HTTP.
- **Webhook**: every delivery needs its `X-GitHub-Delivery` id and a repeated one is ignored for `webhook.replay_seconds`; a repository can cause at most `webhook.max_per_minute` accepted events a minute; the owner in `full_name` must be the watched account; one address is limited to 120 requests a minute in the network mode; an accepted event drops the stored conditional reads of that repository and marks it for the next cycle; a signature header with unusual characters is a plain refusal.
- **MCP server**: a message of the wrong shape (parameters, arguments, id, method) gets an error for that message only, an unexpected defect in a tool is an internal error that does not end the server, and a line over 64 KB is refused.
- **The stored GitHub token is given to `gh` only.** It is no longer put in the environment of the monitor, so `act`, your notification command and every other child cannot inherit it.
- **A GET never writes.** The copy of the daily report in the audit folder is a POST with the one-use token (`/api/sentinel/parte/save`); `?save=1` on the GET is gone.
